title: Hurricane Polo surf reminds me to watch the ocean from the sand
dek: Hurricane Polo sent big swells to Southern California beaches this week, and tonight I am glad to admire the surf from a safe distance.
body: Hurricane Polo stayed far off the coast of Mexico, but it still reached us. Forecasters said south-facing beaches in Southern California could see surf of 4 to 7 feet on Monday and Tuesday, and a coastal flood advisory ran until 5 p.m. today for beaches in Ventura and Los Angeles counties.

The part that stayed with me was a note from forecasters that the surf would be smaller than it was during Hurricane Marie, but the erosion left behind from that storm could make flooding worse. The beach has not had much time to recover, and neither have some of the people who live right along it.

The National Weather Service asked people to stay out of the water because of dangerous rip currents, to keep off the rock jetties, and to protect property in flood-prone spots. Those are simple requests, and they are easy to ignore when the waves look beautiful and the evening is warm.

I understand the pull. Big surf is exciting to see, and a storm you cannot feel on land seems harmless. The ocean does not work that way, and the lifeguards and first responders who go in after people have enough to do this week.
If you head to the coast tomorrow to see what the swell left behind, enjoy it from the sand and give the jetties and the water a pass until the surf settles down.
